title: Permission fidelity harness: canonical fixtures & regression replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As RBAC v2 rolls into production for Dedicated and Private deployments, we need a deterministic way to validate permission matrices across code changes, migrations, and SSO/SAML improvements. Flaky or undetected permission regressions have high customer impact (incidents, data exposure, or operational lockdowns). This ticket scopes a canonical fixtures + regression replay harness that can: (1) snapshot authoritative permission states, (2) run deterministic permission asserts across a matrix of roles/resources/actions, (3) replay real audit logs and synthetic SSO flows to validate enforcement, and (4) gate CI with regression detection and automatic rollback signals.

Goals / Success criteria: 
- Produce a canonical fixture set (JSON snapshots) representing 6 customer archetypes (small SaaS, enterprise multi-org, dedicated-gpu tenant, private-VPC tenant, admin-only accounts, service-accounts).
- Implement a replay harness that consumes audit-event streams and SSO assertions (SAML/OIDC) to exercise permission checks end-to-end.
- Integrate into CI: a failing regression on baseline fixtures must block merges to main and file an automatic incident template.
- Add dashboards & alerts for permission drift: aggregated false-positive rate <= 1% over initial 4-week run.

Technical approach: 
- Canonical fixtures: define a compact canonical format (roles, role-bindings, resources, permission matrix, tenant metadata). Fixtures will be stored in a fixtures/ directory in the permissions repository and versioned by commit SHA.
- Snapshot tooling: CLI tool rbac-snapshot that exports current live permission state from the control plane and normalizes into canonical fixtures. Snapshots can be tagged as CI-baseline or customer-snapshot.
- Replay harness: permission-replay runner that takes a fixture plus an event stream (native audit events or synthetic SAML/OIDC login + action sequences) and asserts allow/deny outcomes against the runtime's authorization endpoint.
- Test vector generation: script to expand fixtures into targeted scenarios including edge-cases: delegated admin impersonation, service-account token refresh, cross-tenant role leakage, and model-inference-specific controls (KV cache access, model log access).
- CI integration: a dedicated workflow (permissions-regression.yml) that runs fast smoke checks for each PR and a nightly exhaustive run. Failures produce an auto-created issue with repro fixture and suggested rollback commit.

Test scenarios to include: 
- Admin-only routes: ensure only admin role can modify org policies across Dedicated and Private modes.
- SAML attribute mapping: validate that SAML group attributes map consistently to role-bindings and that missing attributes produce deny semantics.
- Audit replay: replay a week of anonymized audit logs from staging to validate permission evolution across service upgrades.
- Impersonation flow: verify audit entries for impersonation include original principal and effective principal and that authorization checks use effective principal.
- Migration regressions: validate permission sets pre- and post-migration (schema changes) to ensure parity.

Rollout plan: 
1) Implement canonical format + CLI snapshot tooling (owner: Marco) — 2 sprints.
2) Build replay harness and a minimal set of fixtures for 3 archetypes — 1 sprint.
3) Integrate into PR CI with smoke checks — 1 sprint.
4) Nightly exhaustive runs + dashboards + alerting (owner: Observability) — 2 sprints.

Monitoring & observability: 
- Dashboard: permissions-regression by fixture, failure trend, false-positive rate, avg CI runtime.
- Alert: on regression > 0 for PRs against main or > 2 failures in nightly run.
- Post-fail prototype: attach failing fixture, event stream snippet, and recommended rollback commit.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Fixtures become brittle with frequent API changes. Mitigation: enforce a fixtures linter and add migration helpers to translate old snapshots to new schema.
- Risk: Synthetic SAML flows may diverge from provider behavior. Mitigation: sample and anonymize real SAML assertions from staging to seed generators and run cross-provider smoke tests.
- Risk: CI runtime cost for exhaustive runs. Mitigation: two-tier approach — fast smoke per-PR, nightly exhaustive on dedicated runners.

Notes: This harness is not a replacement for runtime e2e tests; it's focused on permission determinism and regression detection. Close coordination with SRE, Observability, and Identity (SSO) teams is required.
